doc.title: Jerry Dodgion interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 9, 1996

chapter: Early years and arriving in New York
title: Red Norvo, Sinatra and Goodman, then a first New York date with Quincy Jones
summary: After three years with Norvo's quintet, including Las Vegas and Sinatra appearances, Jerome Richardson helped him get his first New York record date with Quincy Jones and Dinah Washington.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: New York, I’d been playing with Red Norvo for three years, with the quintet. And we played all over. We played in Las Vegas a lot. We played for Frank Sinatra for his personal appearances for about a year and a half, and we played with Benny Goodman several times during that time, our first time to Europe. And everything, it was really like a great experience for me. Then when I did stay in New York, the work that I started to do mainly through — I knew Jerome Richardson from San Francisco and we had played together in Gerald Wilson’s band there. And so when I came to New York he encouraged me to come and everything and he helped me a great deal. And on my first recording date when I was here he called me because he was contracting for Quincy Jones. And my very first record date was with Quincy Jones and Dinah Washington. That was, like it was wonderful. So somebody said, “How do you like New York so far?” On my first date it was good. Wonderful.
That’s wonderful. So much of the music business is getting work through friends and establishing contacts.
Sure. In those days the pop music was still jazz oriented more so. Then later on it became more rock & roll, even eighth note oriented. So it changes, it’s changing all the time.
